info.description:
# Local API reference

Import this collection and the accompanying local environment. Base URL defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8001 (no trailing slash). This collection covers every registered canonical /api method/path for active public-site, customer portal, admin and integration modules, plus compatible legacy examples. HTML pages remain thin server-rendered presentation for SEO/design; public page data and structured APIs share the same application layer. This is not an HTML-page wrapper or a disabled-module reactivation.

## Safety first
All non-read methods (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/webhooks) are skipped until allow_writes=true. TOTP setup GET is also guarded because existing behavior can initialize a setup secret. Additional flags default false: allow_messages, allow_destructive, allow_auth_changes, allow_maintenance, allow_private_exports. Payment actions require allow_payment_mutations. Each request can require several flags; no flag is a replacement for server authorization. Payment-state requests also require allow_payment_mutations=true. Remote hosts are skipped unless allow_remote=true; HTTPS is required for remote hosts. These safeguards apply to Send and Collection Runner. Use a current Postman runtime supporting pm.execution.skipRequest and Web Crypto; do not disable scripts or run this in a runtime without those features. No request has been run by creating this collection. Example contacts are fictional. Never run payment completion or webhooks against real orders merely to test connectivity. A sandbox payload still creates database records and can notify administrators.

## Recommended: use Data API v1 from another project's backend
Ask the server operator to issue a short-lived owner-admin token using:
php artisan data-api:token owner@example.test --name=my-project --abilities=customers:read,orders:read,support:read --days=7
Use an actual owner admin email. Maximum token lifetime: 30 days. The owner must already have completed any required password change. Revoke with:
php artisan data-api:token owner@example.test --revoke=TOKEN_ID
No token is supplied or created here. Put the result only in the local environment's data_api_token secret value. Never commit, publish, sync, or export populated secrets; never put this token in browser JavaScript/mobile client code. Use separate minimum-scope tokens for each trusted backend and rotate them before expiry. A stale auth version, non-owner admin, expired/revoked token, or missing ability is rejected. Browser login cookies are not a replacement for this token. Tokens do not bypass browser CSRF, admin 2FA, or HMAC verification.

Data list responses use data plus pagination meta. Optional filters are documented and disabled in each list request's Params tab; enable only the ones you need. Use page >=1 and per_page 1–100 (default 25). updated_since is an inclusive updated_at timestamp, not a deletion/change stream; paginate all pages and handle duplicate records by ID when incrementally syncing. Dates are returned from stored records; fetching data does not start or extend a subscription. Subscriptions are paid package orders, excluding test_paid records. Data is allowlisted: no password hashes, payment signing secrets, or service-login credentials. Customer contact information and support message text remain sensitive; use only for authorized purposes, with appropriate access and retention controls.

## Browser/session-only endpoints
Keep the Postman cookie jar enabled. GET the browser WhatsApp CSRF-token endpoint first; its post-response script saves csrf_token into the selected environment. This is valid only with that same session's cookies. Admin endpoints additionally require your existing authenticated admin session, password/2FA checks, and route permissions. Log in interactively and use a trusted local cookie-sync mechanism if needed; no login/password/2FA bypass is included. Re-fetch CSRF after a session change. Canonical browser APIs return structured 401/403 errors with code and redirect_url when sign-in/password/2FA/confirmation is required; legacy HTML aliases can still redirect. Automatic redirects are disabled so you can inspect the response. Only legacy WhatsApp trial tracking deliberately remains CSRF-exempt; it still uses session consent/payment context.

## HMAC integrations and webhooks
Use separate local secret variables for each integration. Opplexify signatures include the actual requested path, so /api and legacy URLs have different signatures. Scripts render body variables once before hashing so signed bytes match the transmitted body. Tawk and payment webhook formats are not interchangeable with Opplexify. Existing server-side configuration must already be present; this collection does not alter .env or webhook settings. Browse the request descriptions for payload constraints.

## Errors
Data APIs: 401 means authentication failed; 403 means the token/owner/ability is not authorized; 404 means the resource was not found; 422 means validation failed; 429 means throttled. Canonical browser APIs additionally use JSON 401/403 plus code/redirect_url for login, password, 2FA or recent confirmation, and 419 for missing/expired CSRF. Legacy HTML aliases may return 302. Validation is 422; no automatic mutation retry is safe. Integration 401 means signature/timestamp failed, 409 a state/amount/reference conflict, 415 JSON required, and 503 missing integration configuration. Do not share responses containing customer data publicly.

## Scripts
Uses supported Postman pre-request skipRequest and Web Crypto, no external packages. Documentation: https://learning.postman.com/v11/docs/tests-and-scripts/write-scripts/postman-sandbox-reference/pm-execution and https://learning.postman.com/docs/tests-and-scripts/write-scripts/postman-sandbox-reference/pm-require . The collection never logs tokens, cookies, HMAC secrets, or private response bodies.

## Complete browser workflows
Admin: GET /api/browser/admin/bootstrap and /login, manually solve current CAPTCHA and supply authorized local credentials for POST /login only when allow_auth_changes/allow_writes are enabled. Keep cookie jar and refreshed CSRF. Existing role, password, 2FA and ten-minute sensitive-action confirmation checks remain. Customer: GET /api/browser/account/session, request email access explicitly, open the emailed web entry and use the separately signed canonical form action for confirmation. Auth endpoints are not owner Bearer APIs. Do not export passwords, TOTP seeds/codes, recovery codes, signed URLs or cookies.

## Uploads, exports and safe examples
Multipart file rows use empty selections; no local customer files are bundled. Select authorized test fixtures manually. Required file rows and blank identity/credential fields stop a request. PUT/PATCH JSON saves preserve actual registered verbs; multipart update variants use POST with _method=PUT. CSV exports/protected pictures intentionally remain streams and require allow_private_exports=true. Synthetic contacts use example.test and reserved example phone numbers. Do not use them to impersonate real consent. The false confirm/verified/policy flags require a real decision before testing. The same submission_id/draft token must be reused on retries, not regenerated automatically. Disabling guards or exporting populated environments defeats these safety defaults.

## Public pages and existing HTML
/api/v1/site/pages/{page} exposes shared navigation/footer/pricing and page content with locale and SEO metadata. products, configure, providers and published blog data have separate structured endpoints. Session promotion data is only /api/browser/site/context (private no-store). The initial HTML remains server-rendered using those same application services; no self-HTTP or extra blog view increments. Existing localized page URLs and compatible action URLs remain. Frontend writes use the canonical browser APIs; read-only Owner tokens are for authorized server-to-server consumers, not browser admin write credentials.

item.description: Private trusted-server integration. Set opplexify_secret locally only. The GET signature is HMAC-SHA256(method + newline + actual path + newline + Unix timestamp). Write requests can create or change records and send administrative notifications; do not use production data for experimentation.
